research.title: Research the market
steps: Define the customer, job, geography and decision the research must support.
Search official product pages and pricing, then relevant community discussions.
Record source URL, date, claim and whether the author is a maker or customer; deduplicate reposts.
Separate direct competitors, substitutes, customer pain and unsupported assumptions.
Finish with a small validation experiment rather than declaring demand proven.
research.success: A sourced comparison and a testable customer hypothesis.
research.saving: Reuse evidence and existing search access before adding paid collection tools.

validation.title: Validate the next assumption
steps: Choose the assumption most likely to make the idea fail.
Identify people who recently experienced the problem.
Prepare interview questions about actual behavior, existing alternatives and spending.
Draft a small experiment with a success threshold and time limit.
Record results and change the scope based on evidence.
validation.success: Observed behavior supports or challenges a stated assumption.

planning.title: Plan the smallest useful release
steps: State the user outcome and required behavior.
Separate mandatory requirements from preferences.
Define one end-to-end workflow and its acceptance checks.
Identify build-versus-buy decisions and dependencies.
Create a short sequence of reviewable tasks.
planning.success: A bounded release with observable acceptance criteria.
planning.saving: Remove unnecessary features, services and handoffs.

architecture.title: Choose a suitable architecture
steps: Confirm users, workload, data and operational requirements.
Compare the existing setup with feasible alternatives.
Exclude options that fail mandatory requirements; mark unknown evidence explicitly.
Calculate recurring costs and migration effort under identical workload assumptions.
Record the decision, rejected alternatives and reassessment triggers.
architecture.success: A justified decision tied to requirements and cost assumptions.
architecture.saving: Count operations and migration effort as well as provider bills.

design.title: Improve the interface
steps: Capture the intended audience, brand direction and task the screen must support.
Inspect an actual screenshot or running page; do not invent visual findings from source alone.
Identify concrete issues in hierarchy, spacing, typography, states and accessibility.
Prepare a focused implementation prompt and reuse suitable existing components.
Inspect the changed interface at relevant widths and compare it to the brief.
design.success: The edited interface better satisfies the brief with verified usable states.
design.saving: Fix a defined problem before adding another design subscription.

coding.title: Improve the implementation workflow
steps: Read the relevant requirements, existing code and checks.
Reuse the current assistant and project conventions where suitable.
Choose only the skills or integrations needed for this task.
Prepare a bounded change with expected behavior and checks.
Review the result and preserve the useful workflow.
coding.success: A working, checked change that meets the agreed behavior.
coding.saving: Reduce repeated context and overlapping tools.

review.title: Choose a review setup
steps: Define review needs such as security checks, PR feedback, tests and team workflow.
Compare the existing process, local checks and paid review candidates.
Evaluate the same representative change with the candidate approaches.
Record useful findings, missed issues, false positives, time and actual costs.
Configure the selected approach and retain a rollback path.
review.success: Required review coverage with understandable cost and effort.
review.saving: A cheaper approach qualifies only if its review coverage is sufficient.

agents.title: Assess agent cost and effectiveness
steps: Define the task's output and quality criteria.
Check whether a single agent can complete it before introducing parallel work.
If useful, split independent work with explicit inputs and bounded outputs.
Estimate calls, repeated context, model rates, retries and evaluation costs.
Compare results and total cost under the same task conditions.
agents.success: An acceptable result with measured time and cost.
agents.saving: Avoid unnecessary agents, repeated context and retry loops.

database.title: Choose and connect data services
steps: Describe entities, query patterns, tenant boundaries and data sensitivity.
Compare current, bundled and separate services.
Check region, access requirements, backup and recovery needs.
Estimate storage, compute, transfer and operational effort.
Prepare a scoped setup and verify access with representative data.
database.success: A compatible data setup with verified access and recovery assumptions.
database.saving: Compare total service and maintenance cost rather than the database sticker price.

testing.title: Check the behavior that matters
steps: Define observable acceptance criteria and representative edge cases.
Choose deterministic checks where they fit the behavior.
For AI output, define quality criteria and representative examples.
Compare existing and proposed behavior under the same inputs.
Record failures and limits of the sample.
testing.success: Evidence that the change meets its acceptance criteria.
testing.saving: Catch rework early and verify lower-cost alternatives.

automation.title: Automate a repeated handoff
steps: Describe the repeated task, frequency, inputs and side effects.
Compare manual work, a small script and a workflow platform.
Include execution fees, hosting, setup and maintenance in the comparison.
Prepare the smallest useful workflow with retry and error behavior.
Test it on sample inputs and measure actual use.
automation.success: A reliable repeated operation with a clear owner and failure path.
automation.saving: Automate when recurring benefit justifies total effort and cost.

deployment.title: Choose a deployment approach
steps: Check runtime, data, availability and recovery requirements.
Compare the current host with compatible alternatives.
Estimate requests, compute, storage and transfer at current and growth usage.
Prepare deployment, rollback and verification steps.
Check the deployed user journey and observe actual bills.
deployment.success: A verified deployment with understandable operating assumptions.
deployment.saving: Avoid unnecessary infrastructure and expose metered charges.

marketing.title: Plan a focused launch experiment
steps: Define the target buyer, promise and evidence behind the positioning.
Choose a channel where that audience already seeks help.
Prepare landing copy, channel-specific drafts and a small experiment.
Select the minimum analytics needed to judge results.
Compare qualified activation and repeat use with the experiment's cost.
marketing.success: Measured customer response to a specific message and channel.
marketing.saving: Test one channel before buying overlapping marketing subscriptions.

operations.title: Review changes affecting the project
steps: Read current decisions, usage and known problems.
Check relevant vendor pricing, deprecation and incident sources.
Identify which project component is affected and whether action is warranted.
Compare improvement benefit with switching and maintenance costs.
Record action, outcome and the next reassessment trigger.
operations.success: A justified action or a documented decision to keep the current setup.
operations.saving: Remove unused tools and avoid unjustified migrations.

cost.title: Compare total cost
steps: Collect current costs or label assumptions as a forecast.
Keep the workload and evaluation conditions comparable.
Include subscriptions, API usage, hosting, retries and recurring operations.
Show switching effort and payback separately.
Validate quality and compare observed outcomes after a change.
cost.success: Correct arithmetic and a decision that preserves required outcomes.
cost.saving: Only claim verified savings after observing costs and acceptable results.
